elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted Section 5.4: "Notwithstanding Section 5.1, IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL...". IBM is Customer; the right runs to "this Agreement", which satisfies the disjunctive element (Agreement or Order Form). The narrow opener neutralises the retained "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary... for cause" preamble so the new right is operative rather than contradicted.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL" — exactly 30 days, in writing, given by Customer to Vendor. No additional conditions (no consent, no cause, no cure) are attached.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "in which case MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination." The refund obligation is on Vendor (MSL), is expressly pro rata (not merely inferred from a post-termination period), and is triggered by the convenience termination.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 5.1 preamble confines termination to cause for both parties: "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary, this Agreement may be terminated by either Party for cause as follows". Section 4.0's six-month "intent to terminate" notice operates against the automatic twelve-month renewal and is natural-term non-renewal, which is assessed under RENEWAL rather than as a mid-term T4C right. No new Vendor convenience right is created by the insertion, which is one-directional (IBM only).

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The drafted notice period is thirty (30) days, which is the preferred figure and sits outside the 60–90 day fallback band. This is not a defect (the preferred level is met and 30 days is more favourable to Customer); it simply means the fallback checklist is not the completed level.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the inserted Section 5.4 imposes no early-termination fee, penalty or contingent payment on Customer, so there is nothing requiring a cap. SOW Section 6.1's cost-reimbursement language addresses cancellation of individual Purchase Orders, not Agreement-level convenience termination, and is left unchanged.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 5.1 permits termination by either Party only for cause, so Vendor has no convenience right at all — a fortiori stricter than end-of-term only. Caveat for the drafter: Section 4.0's either-party six-month notice does not expressly tie its effective date to the end of the then-current term, so it cannot itself be relied on as an end-of-term restriction; it is treated here as non-renewal under RENEWAL.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: Vendor has no convenience termination right under Section 5.1. To the extent Section 4.0's non-renewal notice were characterised as a Vendor exit, it requires six (6) months' notice, which exceeds 90 days.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met by the single inserted Section 5.4 plus the retained for-cause-only Section 5.1; the fallback level is incomplete only because the notice period (30 days) is below the 60–90 day band, which is more favourable to Customer and therefore not a defect.

Deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" returns false, but on inspection of the rendered operative text this is a mechanical false negative — the text expressly reads "IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL". The operative language, not the regex, controls here; the coverage and minimality gates both pass.

Minimality holds: a single concise insertion for a missing clause, no deletions, no rewriting of Section 5.1, and no extras (no survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no procedures). The drafter correctly omitted "in whole or in part" from the model language, since no Order Form or partial-termination structure in this checklist requires it, and correctly used a narrow "Notwithstanding Section 5.1" rather than a broad override.

Intent is preserved: Sections 5.2, 5.3, Section 4.0's renewal/non-renewal mechanic and cross-reference to Section 5.0, SOW Section 6.1 Purchase Order cancellation and the Parts cost-reimbursement pricing (p0143) all survive without contradiction; the narrow notwithstanding resolves the only tension (the retained "Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement to the contrary... for cause" preamble).

Two drafting points to confirm rather than repair: (i) verify the retained for-cause preamble is in fact numbered Section 5.1 in the executed document, so the new cross-reference is not dangling; (ii) "fees prepaid by IBM" is descriptive rather than a defined term in this manufacturing agreement — consider "amounts prepaid by IBM" if "fees" is not used elsewhere, though this does not defeat the element.
